newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Dry run for Manila APEC summit dampened by rain.
newsitem.headline: Dry run for Manila APEC summit dampened by rain.

text.p: Security preparations for an Asia Pacific summit in the Philippines are encountering minor glitches, a top official in charge of organising the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting said on Tuesday.

Rescue forces, including firemen and ambulance personnel, were slow in reacting to mock emergency calls, but that could be because it was raining heavily, said Juanito Malto, deputy director general of the APEC National Organising Commission.

"There is room for improvement," Malto said, describing reaction to emergency situations by the participants and government agencies during practice sessions at the weekend when the city was battered by torrential rain.
But the core security personnel were quick to respond to the emergency calls, he said.

Heads of state and government from among APEC member economies are due to arrive in the Philippines on November 24 for their annual summit the following day and the government has been worried about security.
There have been no direct threats to the APEC summit but the government is taking no chances as a radical communist group and a splinter Moslem rebel group are active in the country.
Malto said protest rallies would be allowed provided they got the necessary permits from the government.
Philippine police ordered a ban on guns in areas including Manila and Subic Bay where APEC leaders will meet. Subic is 80 km (50 miles) north of Manila.
